result.title: ANCHOR: KL-Anchored Adaptation for Stable Offline-to-Online RL
result.comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Continually Self-Improving Robots. 37 pages
result.summary: Offline-to-online reinforcement learning (RL) follows the pretrain-finetune paradigm: an agent is first pretrained on historical data and then adapted through online interaction. We study offline-to-online adaptation without offline replay, where the agent must improve using only the pretrained model and newly collected experience. A key challenge is to avoid catastrophic failure, a sharp early performance collapse during online fine-tuning, while still achieving strong asymptotic performance. Through controlled experiments, we show that removing offline replay can induce catastrophic failure, while retaining strong conservative regularization from offline RL can suppress final online performance. We also find that common stabilization strategies do not reliably prevent early collapse, and that the critic-side mechanisms we test are insufficient on their own. Motivated by these findings, we propose ANCHOR, a simple adaptation method that anchors the actor to the offline-pretrained policy early in online fine-tuning, anneals this constraint over time, and retains only a small residual conservative critic regularizer. We provide a theoretical interpretation showing that KL anchoring helps preserve critic reliability across nearby occupancy distributions, with a two-phase regret bound explaining when anchoring should be maintained or relaxed. Across FrankaKitchen, AntMaze, and Adroit tasks, ANCHOR substantially reduces catastrophic failure while maintaining strong asymptotic performance. Ablations show that KL annealing and the residual conservative weight are important for balancing early stability and online adaptation, while additional analysis shows that ANCHOR is most beneficial when the pretrained policy contains useful behavior to preserve. Code is available at https://github.com/Cho-Geonwoo/ANCHOR.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究无离线回放的 offline-to-online 强化学习适配，通过控制实验指出早期性能崩塌与保守正则的张力，提出 ANCHOR：在线微调早期将 actor 用 KL 锚定到预训练策略并逐步退火，同时保留少量保守 critic 正则，并给出两阶段 regret 分析，在 FrankaKitchen、AntMaze、Adroit 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先强约束后退火」的 KL 锚定与阶段性约束释放，或可供核查用于 latent 推理模块微调时抑制表示与策略崩塌、兼顾后期适配；但材料不涉及视觉状态、证据获取或 latent 内容使用，仅为训练稳定性层面的远域类比。
